$comment: Licences reviewed deliberately, one entry per package, with the reason it
is acceptable. This is not an allowlist widening: ALLOWED_LICENSES in
scripts/gen-sbom.mjs is unchanged, and every entry here still has to say
what the package is, how it reaches this repository, and whether DeepWatch
redistributes it. A package with no entry still fails the gate.
Everything below arrives through @deepseek-ai/dsh, which @deepwatch/cli
declares as an exact OPTIONAL PEER dependency. pnpm installs optional peers
into this workspace so the CLI can be exercised locally, which is why they
appear in the lockfile at all. No DeepWatch package lists any of them, no
DeepWatch tarball contains any of them, and nothing here is redistributed:
a user's own package manager fetches them from the public registry under
their publishers' terms, exactly as it would for a direct
`npm i @deepseek-ai/dsh`.
The one obligation worth naming: sharp's per-platform packages ship
prebuilt libvips binaries. The Apache-2.0 half is sharp's own glue code;
the LGPL-3.0-or-later half is libvips. Confirmed by reading the files, not
the SPDX string — @img/sharp-win32-x64 contains libvips-42.dll and
libvips-cpp-8.18.6.dll beside sharp's .node addon, and its LICENSE file
carries only the Apache text.
An installer that BUNDLED those binaries rather than fetching them would
take on the LGPL relinking obligation. DeepWatch does not bundle them
today, and docs/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md records that as an open decision
for a future Desktop installer.

packages.component: sharp platform binary for glibc and Windows, bundling prebuilt libvips
packages.reason: Apache-2.0 is sharp's own glue and LGPL-3.0-or-later is the libvips binary it links. The two halves are stated together on Windows and separately on Linux and macOS, which declare only the Apache half — so the combined expression is what the SBOM records, because the payload is the same everywhere. Verified by reading the package rather than the SPDX string: @img/sharp-win32-x64 contains libvips-42.dll and libvips-cpp-8.18.6.dll beside sharp's .node addon, and its own LICENSE file carries only the Apache text. Not present in any DeepWatch package or tarball.

The same libvips payload as the glibc builds, published without a licence field on the platforms that have been read. Recorded as the glibc expression because the contents are the same. Never selected on a supported DeepWatch platform, and not redistributed.

libvips itself. The Windows builds omit the field and the Linux and macOS builds declare LGPL-3.0-or-later, which is the licence of the payload in every one of them — so that is what the SBOM records rather than the absence Windows reports. Not redistributed: a user's own package manager fetches it.
Declares BSD-3-Clause where it is installed, which is Linux only; nothing can read the field on a machine that does not install it. Permissive, and not redistributed.

packages.component: emscripten node-api runtime, the wasm fallback for sharp
packages.reason: Reached only by sharp's wasm32 variant, which is never selected on a supported DeepWatch platform. Published MIT by the emnapi project. Not redistributed.
koffi itself is MIT and on the allowed list; its OpenBSD platform packages carry the same licence and are never installed on a supported DeepWatch platform. Not redistributed.

note: Two fields, and the difference matters. `licenses` is every value a package in this family is known to declare — they differ by platform, and a value outside this list is a licence change nobody reviewed, so the gate fails on whichever machine installs it. `sbomLicense` is the single value the SBOM records everywhere, because pnpm installs only the current platform's optional packages and a document that quoted whatever happened to be on disk would read differently on every machine.
